chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about how to pray (Salat al-Janazah) upon the men and the women. He said: 'The man is placed in front, facing the men, and the women are placed behind the men.'
ai.seo_question: How are men and women arranged during the funeral prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the spatial hierarchy in Salat al-Janazah, establishing that men stand in the front row while women stand directly behind them, mirroring the general congregational prayer arrangement. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of the funeral prayer based on proper gender segregation and order. It reflects the practical application of modesty and leadership roles within the communal worship context as understood by the Ahl al-Bayt.
